title: A census.py dispatch session that stops at its cap leaves its edits in the group's files, so the next part commits unchecked edits and source ids with no row
goal: cmd_dispatch restores each owned file of the part to its content before the session when the run returns no valid result, and prints the files it restored, so a capped or failed session leaves nothing in the tree; a check runs dispatch with a fake claude on PATH that edits an owned file and exits with a cap error, and finds the file unchanged

run: import sys,inspect;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import census;s=inspect.getsource(census.cmd_dispatch);sys.exit(0 if ('snapshot' in s or 'restore' in s) else 1)

repro_reason: the behaviour needs a paid claude -p session that edits a file and then stops at its --max-budget-usd cap; the planted equivalent needs a fake claude on PATH and a census log with open rows, which the fix's check builds
notes: Found in the 2026-10-21 census phase 2 (ST-zpe7qxtv): sessions stopped at their cap after re-pointing facts to new pinned urls; dispatch discarded the result but the edits stayed, the retry and the next part's commit took them, and check.py then found 78 citations of 21 ids with no _sources.csv row (fixed by hand in the census branch, commit 'source rows for facts re-pointed by capped sessions'). The manager's phase-2 driver now snapshots and restores owned files around a failed dispatch as a stopgap. Blocks the next census run's integrity: a capped session's unchecked edits land.
